svg.title: The Lunch Rush Has a Memory Budget
svg.desc: Four-panel comic. 1: Before the noon rush the boss warns that the item numbers will not fit: one item is 768 numbers, times 100 million items, 307 GB. 2: The recommender uses CompresSAE to rewrite each item as a code that keeps only its few strongest numbers; the rest are zero and not stored, yet a close copy of the item can be rebuilt from the code. 3: A user holding item A asks for more like this; to check whether item B is similar, the recommender does not rebuild either item but reads only the few cells of a ready-made table where their kept numbers meet, 9 of 81. 4: Memory drops from 307 GB to 26 GB, 12 times smaller, and the click rate is only 1.35% lower, so the recommender finally gets lunch. Keep the strongest few numbers: 12 times less memory, nearly the same clicks.
svg.text: The Lunch Rush Has a Memory Budget

text.tspan: enough to rebuild a close copy.
